_source: WHO · NICE · ESC/EAS 2021 · BSH · ADA 2024 — no Australian guidelines used
_note: Medications referenced by generic name per NEMSL (National Essential Medicines List of Sri Lanka)

iron_deficiency_anaemia.first_line: Ferrous sulfate 200mg TDS for 3 months after Hb normalises. Investigate and treat underlying cause.
iron_deficiency_anaemia.alternatives: Ferrous gluconate 300mg TDS if GI intolerance. IV iron (ferric carboxymaltose) if malabsorption, IBD, or oral intolerance.
iron_deficiency_anaemia.targets: Hb normalisation within 4 weeks; ferritin target >50 µg/L
iron_deficiency_anaemia.monitoring: FBC + ferritin at 4–6 weeks; continue iron 3 months post-normalisation
iron_deficiency_anaemia.thresholds: Transfusion if Hb <7.0 g/dL (symptomatic) or <8.0 (cardiac disease)

b12_deficiency.first_line: If dietary cause: oral cyanocobalamin 1mg daily. If malabsorption/pernicious anaemia: IM hydroxocobalamin 1mg alternate days ×6 doses, then every 3 months lifelong.
b12_deficiency.note: Check and treat concurrent folate deficiency. Correct before or with B12.

folate_deficiency.first_line: Folic acid 5mg daily × 4 months. Identify cause (dietary, malabsorption, drugs, alcohol).
folate_deficiency.note: Never give folate alone without checking B12 — risk of precipitating subacute combined degeneration of spinal cord

type2_diabetes.first_line: Lifestyle modification (Mediterranean diet, ≥150 min/week exercise, weight loss). Start metformin (500mg BD, titrate to 1g BD if tolerated).
type2_diabetes.second_line_with_cvd_or_ckd: Add SGLT2i (empagliflozin 10mg or dapagliflozin 10mg) — reduces CV events and CKD progression
type2_diabetes.second_line_without_cvd: Add SGLT2i or GLP-1 RA (liraglutide/semaglutide) if weight loss priority; DPP4i if GI intolerance
type2_diabetes.targets: HbA1c ≤48 mmol/mol (lifestyle only) / ≤53 mmol/mol (on medication); BP <130/80
type2_diabetes.monitoring: HbA1c every 3 months until stable, then 6-monthly. Annual: eGFR + uACR + lipids + eye + foot exam
type2_diabetes.south_asian_note: South Asians develop T2DM at lower BMI (~23 kg/m²). Treat pre-diabetes more aggressively. Visceral adiposity common even at normal BMI.

prediabetes.first_line: Intensive lifestyle programme: reduce refined carbohydrates (white rice), increase vegetables/legumes/fibre, ≥150 min/week moderate exercise, target 5–10% weight loss if overweight.
prediabetes.pharmacological: Consider metformin if BMI ≥25 (SA threshold) with additional risk factors
prediabetes.south_asian_note: Pre-diabetes progresses to T2DM faster in South Asians. Monitor at 6 months not 12.

hypertension.targets: General: <130/80 mmHg. Age ≥80: <150/90. CKD with proteinuria: <125/75.
hypertension.first_line_under55: ACE inhibitor (ramipril 2.5–10mg) or ARB (losartan 25–100mg) — especially if diabetes or CKD
hypertension.second_line: Add CCB to ACEi/ARB. Or add thiazide-like diuretic (indapamide 1.5mg MR — preferred over bendroflumethiazide)
hypertension.resistant: Add spironolactone 25mg if K+<4.5, or alpha-blocker/beta-blocker. Investigate secondary hypertension.
hypertension.monitoring: Recheck BP at 2 weeks after new medication. U&E 1–2 weeks after starting ACEi/ARB. Annual check when stable.

dyslipidaemia_primary_prevention.statin_threshold: 10-year CVD risk ≥10% (WHO SEAR-B model) → offer atorvastatin 20mg
dyslipidaemia_primary_prevention.south_asian_consideration: Discuss statin at ≥7.5% in South Asian patients with high-burden lipid/BP/metabolic profile
dyslipidaemia_primary_prevention.targets: ≥40% reduction in non-HDL cholesterol from baseline at 3 months
dyslipidaemia_primary_prevention.monitoring: Lipid profile + LFTs at 6–8 weeks. CK if muscle symptoms.
dyslipidaemia_primary_prevention.titration: If <40% non-HDL reduction: check compliance, increase to atorvastatin 40mg or 80mg

dyslipidaemia_secondary_prevention.targets: LDL <2.0 mmol/L (NICE 2023) AND ≥50% reduction from baseline
dyslipidaemia_secondary_prevention.second_line: Add ezetimibe 10mg if target not reached on max statin
dyslipidaemia_secondary_prevention.monitoring: Lipid profile at 6 weeks → 3 months → annually

hypertriglyceridaemia.tg_1_7_to_5_6: Lifestyle: reduce refined carbohydrates and alcohol, weight loss, ≥150 min/week aerobic exercise. Treat secondary causes (DM, hypothyroid, CKD, medications).
hypertriglyceridaemia.tg_above_5_6: Consider fenofibrate 145mg/day (pancreatitis risk). Rule out secondary causes.
hypertriglyceridaemia.tg_above_11_3: EMERGENCY — hospitalise, restrict dietary fat, insulin infusion if diabetic. Plasmapheresis if extreme.

hypothyroidism.first_line: Levothyroxine: start 50–100 mcg/day (25 mcg if elderly >70 or cardiac disease). Take 30–60 min before food.
hypothyroidism.titration: Titrate every 4–6 weeks. Target TSH 0.5–2.5 mIU/L.
hypothyroidism.monitoring: TFT (TSH + FT4) at 6 weeks after each dose change. Annual TFT once stable.

subclinical_hypothyroidism.treat_if: TSH >10 mIU/L, OR TSH 4–10 with symptoms, OR pregnant (TSH >2.5 in T1)

hyperthyroidism.first_line: Refer endocrinology. Carbimazole (titration or block-and-replace). PTU in pregnancy. Beta-blocker for symptom relief.
hyperthyroidism.monitoring: TFT + FBC (neutropenia risk from carbimazole) at 6–8 weeks

nafld_masld.key_intervention: Weight loss ≥7% body weight — most effective intervention; reduces fibrosis in 50%
nafld_masld.diet: Mediterranean diet; restrict fructose (soft drinks, fruit juice); restrict alcohol completely
nafld_masld.exercise: 150–200 min/week moderate aerobic — reduces hepatic fat independently of weight loss
nafld_masld.monitoring: Annual LFTs + USS. FIB-4 score annually to track fibrosis risk.
nafld_masld.referral: Hepatology if FIB-4 >2.67, or cirrhosis features (low platelets, raised INR, low albumin)

ckd_management.all_stages: BP <130/80. ACEi/ARB if proteinuria (uACR >3). Avoid NSAIDs, nephrotoxins. Low-sodium diet. Mediterranean diet.
ckd_management.g3a_g3b: eGFR 6-monthly, uACR annually. Review medication doses.
ckd_management.g3b_g4: Anaemia screen (EPO if Hb <10). Phosphate + calcium + PTH (CKD-MBD). Bicarbonate if acidosis.
ckd_management.g4_g5: Nephrology referral. CKD-MBD management. Renal replacement therapy planning.
ckd_management.ace_arb_monitoring: Check U&E 1–2 weeks after starting/adjusting. Acceptable creatinine rise ≤30%. Stop if >30% or K+ >5.5.

uti_uncomplicated.upper_uti_pyelonephritis: Co-amoxiclav or ciprofloxacin × 7–14 days. Urine culture essential.
uti_uncomplicated.sri_lanka_note: Check local antibiogram — trimethoprim resistance rising in Sri Lanka. Send MSU for recurrent UTI.

gout.acute: NSAIDs (naproxen 500mg BD) or colchicine (500 mcg BD–TDS) or prednisolone 30mg/day × 5 days
gout.urate_lowering: Allopurinol: start 50–100mg/day; increase monthly; target urate <0.36 mmol/L (ideally <0.30)
gout.dietary: Reduce red meat, beer, fructose-rich drinks, offal. Increase water intake. Weight loss.

hyperkalaemia.k_5_0_to_5_5: Review diet, medications (ACEi/ARB, spironolactone, NSAIDs). Recheck in 1 week.
hyperkalaemia.k_5_5_to_6_0: Urgent ECG. Restrict dietary K+. Stop precipitating drugs.
hyperkalaemia.k_above_6_0: EMERGENCY: IV calcium gluconate 10ml 10% over 10 min (cardiac protection). IV insulin (10 units) + 50ml 50% dextrose. Salbutamol 10–20mg nebulised. Dialysis if refractory.

hyponatraemia.moderate_125_to_130: Treat cause. Max correction 10 mmol/L in first 24h.
hyponatraemia.severe_below_125: Immediate assessment. Endocrinology/nephrology input. 3% saline ONLY if severe neurological symptoms.
hyponatraemia.warning: Overly rapid correction → osmotic demyelination syndrome (central pontine myelinolysis). Max 10 mmol/L per 24h.

vitamin_d_deficiency.deficiency_below_25: Loading regimen: colecalciferol total 300,000 IU over 6–10 weeks (e.g. 50,000 IU weekly × 6). Then maintenance 1000–2000 IU/day.
vitamin_d_deficiency.monitoring: Recheck vitamin D + calcium at 3 months
